summary: Avalonia-specific ReactiveUI guidance with its own startup model and assembly view registration conventions.
recommendedPatterns: Register reactive views from the entry assembly where appropriate.
Use AvaloniaScheduler as the UI scheduler.
avoidPatterns: Do not blindly force the generic RxAppBuilder startup story onto Avalonia.
Do not assume WPF-specific view primitives.
setupSteps: Use Avalonia reactive view base types and view registration helpers.
commonPitfalls: Mixing Avalonia startup guidance with other XAML platforms.
Incorrect scheduler assumptions for Avalonia UI updates.

features: Autofac, DryIoc, Microsoft DI, Ninject, or Splat-only startup
options: Entry, marker, or explicit assembly view scan
Lean Avalonia scheduler or host compatibility surface
packageSelection: Add exactly one ReactiveUI.Avalonia.Autofac, DryIoc, Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection, or Ninject integration when that container owns composition.
Use ReactiveUI.Primitives.Avalonia directly for sequencing in non-ReactiveUI Avalonia libraries.
sourceGeneratorGuidance: Use ReactiveUI.SourceGenerators for Avalonia view models and IViewFor registration before assembly scanning/manual registration where supported.
Use ReactiveUI.Binding generated static paths for AOT/trimming-sensitive bindings; retain runtime Avalonia paths only when dynamic.
compatibilityNotes: UseReactiveUI registers the matching ReactiveUI.Primitives.Avalonia scheduler and platform hooks.
Microsoft DI builds its ServiceProvider during setup, so register all services/views in the callback first.
migrationGuidance: Move manual platform registration to UseReactiveUI/ReactiveUIBuilder, preserving custom registrations through WithRegistration.
Replace System.Reactive dispatcher code with ReactiveUI.Primitives.Avalonia for lean projects; choose a compatibility boundary only when Unit/IScheduler APIs must remain.
